qa_rejections_7d.notes: The kids are never visible: 28 seconds of one distant helicopter hovering over a dark rock pile at dusk from the same high angle, letterboxed and grainy. Nothing on screen looks dangerous, and the source has no closer shot to fix it.

The sinking houseboat is only a dark 4 s FLIR blob; the rest is the same calm top-down basket hoist from the door for about 25 s, which is the routine hoist the viral bar rules out. The cat payoff is nice but cannot carry it, and the source has no other footage.
Blurry, low-contrast footage of a boat that sits level the whole time; no visible sinking, and line 6 says basket over a pump case. Third sinking-boat Short in days. Dropped.

Clean edit, but it is the routine door-cam basket hoist: the water reads as choppy, not as a sixty-knot gale, and several seconds are near-empty sea. The number in the hook is never visible on screen. Dropped.

Great number, weak picture: grainy black-and-white sensor footage of a calm sea, the sailor is never clearly singled out among the Navy crew, and 45 s of near-identical cockpit angles. Nothing on screen shows the danger. Dropped.

Good number, weak picture: for most of the runtime the raft is a speck on calm open ocean or the frame is the helicopter sponson; survivors smile in the basket. Calm routine hoist, no danger visible, and the source has no closer raft footage to fix it with. Dropped.

Grainy black-and-white sensor footage on a fairly calm sea, a glare-only stretch at 18 to 22 s, and the third 'alone in a sinking boat, 12 miles out' Short in three days with the same number hook. Dropped.
640x480 2008 FLIR: the girl and the six people are never visible, the hoist itself is never readable, and render 10 to 20 s is the same sailboat shot. Dropped.

Strong story, weak picture: soft 720p close-ups of the swimmer's suit over surf; the woman, the slope and the failed fire crew attempt are never visible. Same format as the dropped 05-04 Oregon cliff Short.

Isaac boat evacuation is clean but calm: the opening is a woman stepping off a stair, and there is no visible danger beyond rain and a flooded street. It also repeats the hurricane flood type queued from Ike and Florence.
